findings.problem: "Tienes totalmente la razón" is grammatical, but it sounds stiff: speakers say "Tienes toda la razón" (which drops the target word) or "Tienes totalmente razón", and the most natural use of totalmente is in "totalmente de acuerdo".
findings.fix: example.es: Estoy totalmente de acuerdo contigo. / example.en: I totally agree with you.

back.example: You totally have the right / You're totally right.

note: An unprompted learner might answer completamente, but "totally" points clearly to the cognate totalmente, so no hint is needed.
